back: The wavelength of a moving particle: Planck constant divided by its momentum, λ = h/p.
Light: diffraction, interference. Electrons: diffraction rings from graphite.
Light: photoelectric effect. Electrons: deflection by fields, measurable charge and mass.
Randomly oriented graphite crystals; λ comparable with atomic spacing; higher p.d. → shorter λ → smaller rings.
About 0.1 to 0.2 nm: comparable with the wavelength of electrons accelerated through tens to thousands of volts.

front: Why we don't see a ball diffract
back: Its momentum is huge, so λ = h/p is far smaller than any gap.
A magnet moves the diffraction pattern, so it is made by charged particles, not X-rays.
